terms.grammar: adverb, interrogative and relative, of motion away
terms.comment: Unde es? asks where someone is from. As a relative it answers inde, from there. Also of a source: unde hoc?, where did you get that? (Phaedr. 3.7.17).

phrases.latin: unde et quō, Catī? — nōn est mihi tempus
phrases.english: where from and where to, Catius? — I have no time

phrases.latin: juvenēs, quae causa subēgit ignōtās temptāre viās? quō tenditis? inquit; quī genus? unde domō?
phrases.english: “Young men,” he said, “what brought you to try these unknown roads? Where are you going? Who are your people? Where is your home?”

phrases.latin: unde hoc, amīce? — nihil est. — dīc sōdēs tamen
phrases.english: where did you get that, friend? — It’s nothing. — Tell me all the same

phrases.latin: Levāvī oculōs meōs in montēs, unde veniet auxilium mihi.
phrases.english: I lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where my help will come.
